aria: Animated recap of the Suns' 133 to 110 home win over the Clippers: Collin Gillespie's 3-pointer with two-tenths of a second left in the first half, quarter-by-quarter scoring, Jordan Goodwin's 18 points on 6 of 7 from three, the top scorers, how the Suns won, and the next game against Charlotte.
notes: Box score from the Suns' 133–110 home win over the LA Clippers on Nov 10, 2026, from the Covers.com box score, with game details from the AP story carried by 95.3 The Score (KUJZ), Ball Exclusives (via Yardbarker) and theScore. All 133 Suns points and all 110 Clippers points are accounted for in the box score, and the quarter scores add up to both totals (64–47 at the half, matching the AP). Bench points (81–62) are worked out from the box score's starters and match the AP's 81. Field-goal percentages (49 of 88, 38 of 90), threes (22 of 43 and 15 of 44), assists and free throws are the box score's. The 22 threes are a season high, the old mark was 18, and it was Phoenix's biggest win of the season (AP). Records and the Suns' standing are from the site's standings; the next game is from Ball Exclusives.

Biggest lead: Phoenix's 32, at 91–59 on Dillon Brooks' jumper with four minutes left in the third quarter (AP; Ball Exclusives also gives 32). The sources don't give the Clippers' biggest lead, so the reel doesn't show one. Goodwin's 14 minutes are the AP's rounding of the box score's 13:36; he had missed the previous four games with a right calf injury (AP). Kennard's 14 points were a season high (AP).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Collin Gillespie's 3-pointer with two-tenths of a second left in the second quarter, which put the Suns up 64–47 at halftime (AP); the Suns' own account called it a deep three to end the first half (via theScore), and the line score confirms 64–47. The recaps don't describe how he got the shot, so it is drawn as the template's plain pull-up. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Phoenix Suns or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The shooter in the play of the game is drawn to Gillespie’s listed 6-foot-1 and 195 pounds (Basketball-Reference and FOX Sports), with arms at his height because no wingspan is reported, in the Suns' home white with No. 12 (FOX Sports roster). His look hasn't been approved yet, so he is drawn as a team-colour silhouette. It is an original figure with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
